Part 3 — Reading

20 points total · Read the passage once or twice, then answer all 12 questions below it.

A Cup of Coffee in Istanbul

Mona woke up early. The sun was bright, and the sky was blue. She smiled and got out of bed.

Mona was in Istanbul for a short holiday. She wanted to visit the old city and drink Turkish coffee.

After breakfast, Mona walked to a small café near her hotel. She ordered a cup of coffee and a piece of cake. The waiter was friendly, and the café was cozy.

While she waited, Mona noticed an elderly man reading a newspaper at the next table. He looked completely absorbed in the article, occasionally shaking his head at what he read.

Mona started a conversation with him. He explained that the news these days was rather disheartening, filled with stories of political tension and economic uncertainty. Yet, he said, he still found comfort in small pleasures — a good cup of coffee, a quiet morning, a stranger willing to talk.

Mona was struck by his perspective. She had always believed that happiness depended on big achievements: a promotion, a new house, a perfect vacation. But listening to this man, she began to reconsider.

Perhaps, she thought, fulfillment isn't a destination you arrive at, but a habit you cultivate — a deliberate choice to notice the ordinary moments that make up most of our lives.

As she left the café that afternoon, Mona felt strangely lighter, as though a subtle shift had occurred in how she viewed her own ambitions.

She continued her walk through the winding streets of the old city, past vendors selling spices and carpets, their voices blending into a rhythmic hum. The city, she realized, was teaching her something no guidebook ever could.
